EE5203 Lab 8 Guide

ADC: read a potentiometer and a light sensor, then set the LD2 brightness - Basri Erdogan

Mission: Read a potentiometer on A0 with ADC1 and show the reading in millivolts in Live Watch. Then let the potentiometer set the brightness of LD2 through the TIM2 PWM of Lab 7, with no HAL_Delay() anywhere. Then add a light sensor on A1 and turn LD2 into a night-light.

Prepare before class

Learning objectives

By checkoff time, you can:

  1. configure ADC1 for two analog pins: 12 bits, single conversion, 84-cycle sampling;
  2. read a channel with start, wait, read, on the 10 ms tick;
  3. convert an ADC value to millivolts and to a PWM duty with integer arithmetic;
  4. read two sensors with one converter and show the channel in the SFR view.

Hardware and files

Item Value
Board Nucleo-F401RE: LD2 is on PA5, which is also TIM2_CH1
Clock HSI, PLL off (CubeMX step 2): 16 MHz; ADC clock = 16 MHz ÷ 2 = 8 MHz
Timer TIM2: 1 ms tick and PWM on channel 1, PSC 15, ARR 999, as in Lab 7
Potentiometer 10 kΩ: outer legs to 3V3 and GND, middle leg to A0 (PA0, ADC1_IN0)
Light sensor from Checkpoint C on: 10 kΩ resistor from 3V3 to A1, LDR from A1 to GND (PA1, ADC1_IN1)
ADC ADC1: 12 bits, single conversion, sampling time 84 cycles (12 µs for one reading)
Project new CubeMX project EE5203_L08_<studentnumber>, built in VS Code
File you edit main.c, only inside the USER CODE regions

The same two circuits as diagrams:

One jumper takes 3V3 to the + row of the breadboard and one takes GND to the − row. An analog pin must stay between 0 V and 3.3 V: never connect the 5V pin to the breadboard in this lab.

Configure in CubeMX

Start of the session: if C:\Work\<studentnumber> does not contain your Lab 7 project, copy all your project folders from H:\EE_Labs into it first.

  1. STM32CubeMX: Board Selector → NUCLEO-F401RE → accept the default initialization.
  2. Clock Configuration tab: System Clock Mux = HSI; AHB, APB1 and APB2 prescalers = /1. Every box on the right reads 16, as in Lab 7.
  3. PA5: click the pin and choose TIM2_CH1, as in Lab 7. Do this before step 4.
  4. Timers → TIM2: Clock Source = Internal Clock; Channel1 = PWM Generation CH1. Parameter Settings: Prescaler 15, Counter Period 999; PWM Generation Channel 1: Mode PWM mode 1, Pulse 0.
  5. PA0 and PA1: click PA0 and choose ADC1_IN0; click PA1 and choose ADC1_IN1. Both pins turn green.
  6. Analog → ADC1 → Parameter Settings: Resolution 12 bits (15 ADC Clock cycles) and Continuous Conversion Mode Disabled are the defaults: check them. Open ADC_Regular_ConversionMode → Rank 1: Channel = Channel 0, Sampling Time = 84 Cycles. The default is 3 Cycles: change it.
  7. System Core → NVIC: enable TIM2 global interrupt. The ADC needs no interrupt.
  8. Project Manager: name EE5203_L08_<studentnumber>, location C:\Work\<studentnumber>, Toolchain/IDE = CMake → Generate Code.
  9. Copy C:\Users\Public\EE5203_template\.vscode into the project folder, as in every lab. (Own laptop: use Set Up STM32Cube project(s), as in Lab 5.)
  10. Verify, do not add: in main.c, MX_ADC1_Init() with ADC_RESOLUTION_12B, ADC_CHANNEL_0 and ADC_SAMPLETIME_84CYCLES, and MX_TIM2_Init() with TIM_OCMODE_PWM1; in stm32f4xx_hal_msp.c, HAL_ADC_MspInit() with GPIO_PIN_0|GPIO_PIN_1 and GPIO_MODE_ANALOG, and GPIO_AF1_TIM2 (PA5); in stm32f4xx_it.c, TIM2_IRQHandler().

Step 3: click pin PA5 and choose TIM2_CH1. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Step 4: TIM2 with PWM on channel 1. Check the boxed rows. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Step 5: click pin PA0 and choose ADC1_IN0, then PA1 and ADC1_IN1. IN0 and IN1 are then ticked in the ADC1 list. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Step 6: Analog, ADC1, Parameter Settings. Open Rank 1 with the small arrow and set Sampling Time to 84 Cycles. Click the picture for full size. Esc or ✕ closes.

Checkpoint A - The potentiometer in millivolts

Put the potentiometer on the breadboard and wire it as in the figure: outer legs to the + row (3V3) and the − row (GND), middle leg to A0. Fill the Predicted columns of the table below before you build. Three additions:

  1. In USER CODE BEGIN PV, the millisecond counter of Lab 7 and two results. They are global variables, so Live Watch can show them:

    volatile uint32_t g_ms = 0;
uint32_t raw_pot = 0, mv_pot = 0;     /* potentiometer: ADC value and millivolts */

  2. In USER CODE BEGIN 4, the tick callback, as in Lab 7:

    void HAL_TIM_PeriodElapsedCallback(TIM_HandleTypeDef *htim)
{
    g_ms++;                               /* TIM2 update: every 1 ms */
}

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 2, start the tick; in USER CODE BEGIN 3, one reading every 10 ms: start, wait, read, then convert:

    /* USER CODE BEGIN 2 */
HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT(&htim2);                /* 1 ms tick: g_ms */
uint32_t t_adc = 0;

/* USER CODE BEGIN 3 */
if ((g_ms - t_adc) >= 10U) {                  /* every 10 ms */
    t_adc = g_ms;
    HAL_ADC_Start(&hadc1);                    /* start one conversion      */
    HAL_ADC_PollForConversion(&hadc1, 2);     /* wait for EOC, about 12 us */
    raw_pot = HAL_ADC_GetValue(&hadc1);       /* read ADC1->DR             */
    mv_pot  = (raw_pot * 3300u) / 4095u;      /* multiply first            */
}

  4. Build (Ctrl+Shift+B). In .vscode/launch.json, below "runToEntryPoint": "main", paste the line "liveWatch": { "enabled": true, "samplesPerSecond": 4 }, as in Lab 7. Start the debugger (F5), Continue. In Run and Debug, open Cortex Live Watch (own laptop: STM32Cube Live Watch), click +, add raw_pot and mv_pot.

Potentiometer position Predicted raw_pot Predicted mv_pot Measured raw_pot Measured mv_pot
fully toward GND
about the middle
fully toward 3V3

Evidence for Checkpoint A: raw_pot follows the potentiometer from about 0 to about 4095, and mv_pot from about 0 to about 3300. Pause: in the SFR view ADC1->DR holds the same number as raw_pot; GPIOA->MODER bits 1:0 read 11 (PA0 is analog); SMP0 in ADC1->SMPR2 reads 100 (84 cycles). Copy the table into USER CODE BEGIN Header as a comment. Screenshot A_live.png: Live Watch with raw_pot and mv_pot.

Checkpoint B - The potentiometer sets the LD2 brightness

The reading becomes a PWM duty: 0 … 4095 is scaled to 0 … 1000. The top value is ARR + 1: LD2 fully on, the +1 rule of Lab 7. Three additions:

  1. In USER CODE BEGIN PV, below the potentiometer variables:

    uint32_t duty = 0;                    /* 0 ... 1000, written to TIM2->CCR1 */

  2. In USER CODE BEGIN 2, below the tick line, start the PWM:

    HAL_TIM_PWM_Start(&htim2, TIM_CHANNEL_1);     /* PWM on PA5 (LD2) */

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 3, inside the 10 ms block, below the mv_pot line:

    duty = (raw_pot * 1000u) / 4095u;             /* 0 ... 1000 */
TIM2->CCR1 = duty;

Evidence for Checkpoint B: the potentiometer moves LD2 from dark to fully on with no steps. Add duty to Live Watch: it goes from 0 to 1000. Pause: TIM2->CCR1 in the SFR view holds the same number as duty. No HAL_Delay() in main.c. Predict, then check: the potentiometer is at the middle. What is duty? Then turn the potentiometer slowly from one end to the other. In which half of the turn does the brightness change more? Write one sentence: why? (Lab 7, the level table.) Screenshot B_duty.png: Live Watch with raw_pot, mv_pot and duty, and your USER CODE BEGIN 3 lines.

Checkpoint C - A light sensor on a second channel

Add the light sensor as in the figure: the 10 kΩ resistor from the + row (3V3) to A1, the LDR from A1 to the − row (GND). The potentiometer stays on A0. ADC1 converts one channel at a time, so a function selects the channel before each conversion. Three changes:

  1. In USER CODE BEGIN 0, the function:

    uint32_t adc_read(uint32_t channel)
{
    ADC_ChannelConfTypeDef s = {0};
    s.Channel      = channel;
    s.Rank         = 1;
    s.SamplingTime = ADC_SAMPLETIME_84CYCLES;
    HAL_ADC_ConfigChannel(&hadc1, &s);            /* select the channel */
    HAL_ADC_Start(&hadc1);
    HAL_ADC_PollForConversion(&hadc1, 2);
    return HAL_ADC_GetValue(&hadc1);
}

  2. In USER CODE BEGIN PV, below duty:

    uint32_t raw_ldr = 0;                 /* light sensor: ADC value */

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 3, the 10 ms block now reads both sensors, and the light sensor sets the duty:

    if ((g_ms - t_adc) >= 10U) {                  /* every 10 ms */
    t_adc = g_ms;
    raw_pot = adc_read(ADC_CHANNEL_0);        /* potentiometer, PA0 */
    raw_ldr = adc_read(ADC_CHANNEL_1);        /* LDR,  PA1 */
    mv_pot  = (raw_pot * 3300u) / 4095u;
    duty    = (raw_ldr * 1000u) / 4095u;      /* dark room, bright LD2 */
    TIM2->CCR1 = duty;
}

Evidence for Checkpoint C: add raw_ldr to Live Watch. Cover the LDR with your hand: raw_ldr rises and LD2 gets brighter. Shine your phone light on it: raw_ldr falls and LD2 gets dimmer. The potentiometer still changes raw_pot, but it does not change raw_ldr or LD2. Pause: SQ1 in ADC1->SQR3 reads 1, because channel 1 was converted last. In USER CODE BEGIN Header, write one sentence: why does a dark room give a larger raw_ldr? Use the divider. Screenshot C_night.png: Live Watch with raw_pot, raw_ldr and duty.

Checkpoint D - The potentiometer sets a servo angle (optional, not graded)

Only if your kit has a servo and time remains. TIM3 makes the 50 Hz servo signal on PA6 (D12), as in the Lab 7 extension. Predict first: raw_pot = 1024 gives which TIM3->CCR1, and which angle?

  1. CubeMX: click PA6 and choose TIM3_CH1. Timers → TIM3: Clock Source = Internal Clock; Channel1 = PWM Generation CH1; Prescaler 15, Counter Period 19999, Pulse 1500. Generate Code: your USER CODE lines stay.

  2. Wiring: servo signal (orange) to D12, red to 5V, brown to GND. The servo is the only part on the 5V pin: wire it straight to the servo, never to the breadboard rows.

  3. In USER CODE BEGIN 2, start the servo signal; in USER CODE BEGIN 3, inside the 10 ms block, one more line:

    HAL_TIM_PWM_Start(&htim3, TIM_CHANNEL_1);          /* in USER CODE BEGIN 2 */

TIM3->CCR1 = 500u + (raw_pot * 2000u) / 4095u;     /* in the 10 ms block: 500 ... 2500 us */

Evidence for Checkpoint D: the potentiometer turns the servo from one end to the other, and TIM3->CCR1 in the SFR view matches your prediction. If the servo buzzes at an end, it is at its stop (Lab 7): stay a little inside that end.

Individual extension - Fix an AI-written night-light (optional, click)

Optional. Open this only after Checkpoint C is shown and time remains (instead of Checkpoint D, or after it). A classmate asked an AI tool for an on/off night-light. The code compiles, but it does not work on your board. Call night_light() from your 10 ms block instead of the raw_ldr, duty and CCR1 lines of Checkpoint C.

void night_light(void) {
    ADC_ChannelConfTypeDef s = {0};
    s.Channel = ADC_CHANNEL_4;          // LDR input
    s.Rank = 1;
    s.SamplingTime = ADC_SAMPLETIME_3CYCLES;
    HAL_ADC_ConfigChannel(&hadc1, &s);
    HAL_ADC_Start(&hadc1);
    HAL_ADC_PollForConversion(&hadc1, 2);
    raw_ldr = HAL_ADC_GetValue(&hadc1);
    if (raw_ldr > 2000u)
        TIM2->CCR1 = 1000;              // on
    else
        TIM2->CCR1 = 0;                 // off
}
  1. LD2 ignores your hand. Pause after a read. Find SQ1 in ADC1->SQR3 and compare its channel number with the Hardware table. Fix the code. Screenshot: E_sqr3.png.
  2. The light reading follows the potentiometer. Keep the light steady and turn the potentiometer end to end. Write the lowest and highest raw_ldr. Change the sampling time to 84 cycles and repeat.
Sampling time Lowest raw_ldr Highest raw_ldr Spread
3 cycles
84 cycles
  1. Switch once, without flicker. Your switching point is T = 1500 + 10 × (last two digits of your student number). LD2 turns on above T + h and off below T − h. Choose h larger than your 84-cycle spread. Shade the LDR slowly: LD2 must switch once.

Evidence: E_sqr3.png; the table, T and h in USER CODE BEGIN Header, with one sentence on why h must be larger than the spread; the slow-shade demo.

Acceptance checklist

Individual oral check

  • raw_pot reads 1241. How many millivolts is that, and what is duty?
  • Why is the scale factor 1000 and not 999?
  • The sampling time is 84 cycles and the ADC clock is 8 MHz. How long is one conversion?
  • raw_pot and raw_ldr are read on the same tick. Are they from the same instant? Why?
  • Why does covering the LDR make raw_ldr larger? What changes if the LDR and the resistor swap places?

Submit

Submit main.c as it is at the end of the session, A_live.png, B_duty.png and C_night.png.

Marks (10): pre-lab quiz on CATS 1 · A potentiometer in millivolts with SFR evidence 2 · B potentiometer sets the LD2 brightness 2 · C two channels and the night-light 3 · oral check (one question) 2. Checkpoint D and the extension are optional and not graded.

If you are stuck

Walk the signal from left to right and fix the first silent stage: potentiometer voltage on A0 → PA0 analog (MODER bits 1:0 = 11) → g_ms growing → the 10 ms block runs (breakpoint) → ADC1->DR changing → raw_pot → duty → TIM2->CCR1 → LD2. raw_pot stays at 0 or at 4095? The middle leg of the potentiometer is not on A0, or an outer leg is not on 3V3 or GND. raw_pot never changes from its first value? g_ms is frozen: HAL_TIM_Base_Start_IT() is missing, or TIM2 global interrupt is not enabled in NVIC (step 7). mv_pot is 0 until the very end of the turn? The division comes before the multiplication. LD2 stays dark in Checkpoint B? HAL_TIM_PWM_Start() is missing, or PA5 is still GPIO_Output in the .ioc (step 3). raw_ldr follows the potentiometer? A1 is not connected, or the sampling time is still 3 cycles (step 6, or the line in adc_read()). LD2 gets dimmer when you cover the LDR? The LDR and the resistor have swapped places. LD2 is never fully dark in a bright room? Correct: raw_ldr is not 0 in light. The extension turns this into a clean on/off switch. Live Watch empty? Add the liveWatch line, then restart the debugger (Shift+F5, F5).
